clue.text: A player with a big following

definitions.text: A player with a big following

parts.words: A player with a big following
parts.note: the musician of the folk tale whose piping led the rats and then the town's children away behind him, a literal following

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer boasts a huge fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big following' suggests fame and fans; the actual following was a procession of rats and children trailing after a piper in the Hamelin legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hamelin piper was a musician whom crowds literally walked behind, so he is a player with a following.

clue.text: Raised hint about officer's loopy lace

indicators.note: the turned word goes about, around, the officer's abbreviation
in a down entry raised means the word for hint is written upward, back to front

parts.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
CO is the usual abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A tip-off about an officer concerns some fancy lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns TIP upward into PIT, and 'about' puts CO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Picot is a small ornamental loop worked into the edge of lace or ribbon, so it is lace with loops.

clue.text: Like a puzzle (cryptic)?

definitions.meaning: puzzling, mysterious, hard to make out
obscure in meaning, as a cryptic remark is

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe something baffling whose meaning is hidden, as a riddle or an obscure remark is.

clue.text: With certain digits going in?

parts.note: digits here are toes rather than numbers, and going in means pointing inward when walking

explanation.surface: A question about some numbers being entered into a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digits' looks like numbers and 'going in' like data entry; the digits are the toes on a foot, turned inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with this gait walks with the feet turned in, so the toes point inward.

clue.text: It's difficult living near this line

definitions.text: It's difficult living near this line

parts.words: It's difficult living near this line
parts.note: the line is the income threshold below which a household counts as poor, not a railway or border

explanation.surface: A complaint about the hardship of living beside a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests a railway track; it is the official income threshold, and 'difficult living' means a hard life on little money.
explanation.definitionFit: The poverty line is the minimum income level, so people near it find living hard.

clue.text: Objects to offers first off

indicators.note: first off tells us the opening letter of the word for offers is removed

parts.note: presents means offers or gives formally

explanation.surface: Someone objects to offers before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' reads as 'to begin with'; it removes the first letter, P, from PRESENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to take objection to it, feeling bitter about it.

clue.text: Bit of a fight

explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is both a small fragment of something and, informally, a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: Society's game for a game

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for society
nap is a card game, short for Napoleon

explanation.surface: A society chooses one game in exchange for another.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP is an old trick-taking card game also called Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game in which players call out when two matching cards appear.

clue.text: Money in myrrh in olden times?

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: A question about whether myrrh served as currency long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across myrRH IN Olden. 'Times' merely completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for cash.

clue.text: Developed ropy trade in exploiting others

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have been worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A grubby kind of commerce grows up around exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' rearranges ROPY and TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory person or firm preys on others for gain, taking advantage of them.

clue.text: A hundred fish hold fast

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A hundred fish stick firmly together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly and not let go.

clue.text: Imagine crushed suit mainly in travelling-case

indicators.note: in places the crushed letters within the case

parts.note: a valise is a small travelling bag or case

indicators.note: crushed suggests the letters are squashed into a new order
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Picture a suit squashed into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' cuts SUIT to SUI, 'crushed' rearranges it as ISU, and 'in' puts that inside VALISE after its V.
explanation.definitionFit: To visualise is to form a mental picture of something.

clue.text: I get the shakes: a doctor's coming in unusual routine

indicators.note: coming in shows one group of letters entering the other
unusual signals the letters of routine in an odd order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone shaken by a doctor arriving during an odd daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges ROUTINE into TOURINE, and 'coming in' slips A and MB inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument with jingles in its frame, it is played by being shaken, so it speaks of shaking.

clue.text: Garment of long ago taken up in return

indicators.note: in an across clue up joins in return in turning the letters backwards
in return points to letters held in the words and read back the other way

explanation.surface: An old garment is taken back as a return.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, agO Taken contains the word; 'of long' completes the picture of an ancient garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Press on debts with student year in an artificial way

parts.note: to spur is to urge on or press forward
IOUs are written promises of money owed
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is pushed hard about their debts in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Spuriously means falsely or in a fake, not genuine, manner.

clue.text: Where in France tasty cocktail's to last longer

parts.note: ou is the French word for where

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A French bar's tasty cocktail keeps someone there late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' mixes TASTY into TSTAY after the French OU.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain beyond an expected time, as in outstaying a welcome.

clue.text: Old boy tied up, constrained legally

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
ligated means bound or tied, as a surgeon ties a vessel

explanation.surface: A former pupil is tied up and held by law.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligated means bound by duty or a legal requirement to do something.

clue.text: The leader with authority's to drink (concerning doctor)

parts.note: sup means to drink in small mouthfuls
re means about or concerning
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A boss is off for a drink, with a note about a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation.

clue.text: Administration of the most exclusive kind

definitions.meaning: the branch of government or management that carries policy out
describing a superior class of product, such as a luxury car or travel class

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the managing arm of an organisation and also describes upmarket goods aimed at senior people.

clue.text: Stand for Speaker?

parts.note: stand for looks like represent, as in standing for election, but means a stand used by a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone asks who will stand for the post of Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for Speaker' looks like running for the chair of a parliament; it is a reading desk that holds a speaker's notes.
explanation.definitionFit: This sloped desk on a pedestal holds the text a reader or preacher speaks from.

clue.text: The most intimate see RN at work.

indicators.note: at work puts the letters to work, rearranging them, with at counted among the fodder

explanation.surface: An intimate friend watches the Royal Navy busy at its job.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy. 'Work' rearranges SEE, RN and AT; 'at' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest can mean closest in relationship, the dearest and most intimate.

clue.text: Buffet kind of light attached to vehicle

indicators.note: attached to puts the light's letters after the vehicle's

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: A light is bolted onto a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a flare named after its inventor. 'Buffet' reads as a verb, to batter, but is the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant or meal where roast meat is carved and diners serve themselves.

clue.text: … and how boat is made?

parts.note: a boat is a craft, so a vessel made into a boat has been turned into a craft, the -ed form of that noun

explanation.surface: Following the carvery clue, a question about boat building.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue before. The word means skilfully made, and also reads as 'made into a craft', a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilfully made by hand, and literally given the form of a craft, which is a vessel.

clue.text: A number of stars lacking two unknowns for a sporting occasion

indicators.note: lacking means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a galaxy is a huge system of stars
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A star-studded event goes ahead without two mystery guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing X and Y, the algebraic unknowns, from GALAXY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion, in Britain often a swimming or athletics meeting.

clue.text: What one doesn't want to be when roles become changed

definitions.text: What one doesn't want to be

indicators.note: become changed signals the letters of roles taking a new order

explanation.surface: Nobody wants to find their roles switched around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become changed' rearranges ROLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody competes hoping to be beaten, so the one who fails is what one hopes not to become.

clue.text: Registered, but rarely located one around good university

indicators.note: around shows the anagram wraps round the other letters
rarely, meaning in an unusual way, signals the letters rearranged

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A rarely found graduate has been put on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' rearranges LOCATED and A into CATALOED; 'around' wraps that round G and U, slipped in before ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be catalogued is to be entered on a list or record, which is what registered means.

clue.text: Put off, being housed in badly-made terrace

indicators.note: being housed in tells us the letters live inside the following words

explanation.surface: A badly built terrace of houses deters buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across badly-maDE TERrace; a terrace is a British row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting, to put them off.

clue.text: Ridiculous last letter to some

parts.note: z is the last letter of the alphabet
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Writing a final letter to someone is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last letter' sounds like a final piece of correspondence; it is Z, the end of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means comically eccentric or absurd.

clue.text: Will's to examine me in a number of books

parts.note: to test is to examine

indicators.note: in places the word me inside the other letters

parts.note: NT, the New ..., is a collection of books of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A will says to examine me among many books.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes inside A and NT to make AMENT, after TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal document disposing of one's property after death, a will.

clue.text: Speedy writer

definitions.meaning: Jonathan ..., the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fast, and it is also the surname of the author of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Headwear for the race?

definitions.meaning: a stiff felt hat with a rounded crown, the American name for a bowler
the famous flat horse race run at Epsom

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a bowler hat in American usage and to the Epsom horse race.

clue.text: Debt ready to be settled for popular children's item

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters are rearranged into order, as a debt is cleared

explanation.surface: A debt that must be paid for a popular toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be settled' reads as paying off a debt; it rearranges DEBT and READY.
explanation.definitionFit: This stuffed toy bear is a favourite plaything of young children.
